content.problemStatement:
Write a function that returns the longest common prefix string shared among an array of strings. If there is no common prefix, output an empty string "".

The longest common prefix is the longest string that is a prefix of every string in the input array. The function should be case-sensitive and treat digits and lowercase letters as distinct characters.

Design an algorithm that runs in O(n * m) time where n is the number of strings and m is the length of the common prefix, and uses O(m) extra space for the result.
constraints: Each non-empty strs[i] contains only lowercase English letters and digits (characters in [a-z0-9]).
Expected time complexity: O(n * m); expected extra space: O(m).
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array containing one array of strings: [["str1","str2",...]]. Example: [["flower","flow","flight"]]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialized string representing the longest common prefix, e.g. "fl"
notes: Return the longest prefix common to all strings in the input array.
If any string is empty, the result is the empty string.
The input may contain digits and lowercase letters; matching is exact and case-sensitive.
A straightforward approach is to use the first string as a reference and compare characters position-by-position across all other strings.

sampleTestCases.explanation: The longest prefix common to all strings is "fl".
There is no common prefix among the input strings, so return an empty string.

solution.approach: Use the first string as a reference and compare characters position-by-position across all other strings. Stop at the first mismatch or when the reference string ends. Return the prefix up to that point. This approach runs in O(n * m) time where n is the number of strings and m is the length of the common prefix, and uses O(m) space for the result.
